rules.source: Lei n.º 58/2019 of 8 August — Portugal's GDPR execution law (not a transposition, since GDPR is directly applicable, but a supplementary law filling the discretion GDPR leaves to member states); the Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados (CNPD) is the designated supervisory authority. https://www.garrigues.com/en_GB/new/new-portuguese-data-protection-act

Lei n.º 58/2019 — non-compliance with Portuguese data protection law can trigger criminal, civil, and administrative liability (beyond GDPR's own administrative fines), and affected individuals have a statutory right to compensation from the controller/processor for damage suffered. https://www.recordinglaw.com/world-laws/world-data-privacy-laws/portugal-data-privacy-laws/
Lei n.º 109/2009, de 15 de setembro (Lei do Cibercrime), Article 6 acesso ilegítimo — https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/lei/109-2009-489693
rules.retrieved_snippet: Diário da República / secondary summaries: the Cybercrime Law transposes Framework Decision 2005/222/JAI and adapts domestic law to the Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime; Article 6 criminalises unauthorised access to a computer system and the consolidated text includes amendments from Lei n.º 79/2021 and Decreto-Lei n.º 125/2025. Penalty figures were only seen in a partial excerpt and are not stated here.

rules.source: Lei n.º 24/96, de 31 de julho (Lei de Defesa do Consumidor) — https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/lei/24-1996-406882
rules.retrieved_snippet: Diário da República: establishes the legal regime for consumer protection and repeals Lei n.º 29/81; Article 1 places the duty to protect consumers on the State, the Autonomous Regions and local authorities; amended many times including Lei n.º 47/2014 (Directive 2011/83/EU) and Lei n.º 28/2023. Portugal has no single consumer code; rules are spread across several laws.

rules.source: Lei n.º 27/2021, de 17 de maio (Carta Portuguesa de Direitos Humanos na Era Digital) — https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/lei/27-2021-163442504
rules.retrieved_snippet: Charter of digital rights: states that fundamental rights apply fully in cyberspace and guarantees free access to the Internet; its original Article 6 on disinformation was heavily criticised and largely repealed by an amendment approved on 21 July 2022 (leaving only its first paragraph). Current consolidated text not retrieved.
